content.title: States: Hover, Focus, and More
content.hook: Sometimes an element should look different because of its current state. CSS can target states with pseudo-classes.

content.question: Which rule should change a button only while the pointer is over it?

feedback.correct: The pseudo-class name describes the state.
feedback.incorrect: The pseudo-class name describes the state.

content.question: A learner removes the visible focus outline because “it looks cleaner.” What is the problem?

options.text: Keyboard users may lose a visible indication of which element is focused.

feedback.correct: A state indicator can be functional. Focus visibility helps people navigate and understand where input will go.
feedback.incorrect: A state indicator can be functional. Focus visibility helps people navigate and understand where input will go.

content.question: Which is the better engineering choice?

options.text: Style hover only because everyone uses a pointer.
Treat interaction states as part of the interface, including a visible focus state.
Use a state only when it looks fashionable.

feedback.correct: State styling is part of interaction design and accessibility.
feedback.incorrect: State styling is part of interaction design and accessibility.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: Senior habit: When styling an interactive control, ask what it looks like before, during, and after input—not just when it is idle.
